issues: Covers up 31 week on week, down 17 year on year; spend per head up slightly despite heavy ramen promotions.
Sales down 740 GBP week on week and nearly 4,000 GBP year on year, but over 4,500 GBP ahead of target with over 4,500 GBP of discounts.
Delivery machine blip Friday 16:00 to 17:00; prep time flagged as a major red priority to bring down permanently.
Refunds from a missing takoyaki and a rider delivering to the wrong customer.
Food cost up on frozen ramen ordering; Haru to cut LWBC ordering from twice to once a week.
Google reviews: David won the cash incentive for named reviews.
Onboarding: Bishall starts tomorrow (from Manchester or London).
Compliance 99%; maintenance: unauthorised light fixture, doors awaiting repaint (paint selection), toilet tops awaiting repair.
Upcoming: book launch, student frozen ramen promo, large local business pre order launch expected over 2,000 GBP.
Region: food spend target temporarily raised to 26% until current promotions end (Matthew Jenner).
Region: hats or hairnets mandatory for all staff to prevent food contamination.
Region: menu to be redesigned with spice levels built into all ramen dishes and free chillies removed.
Region: GM and HC meeting notes must run through Google Meet so Gemini takes the notes; budget router templates updated, Monday dates must be entered correctly.
Covers reached 1,447 (up 2.1% week on week, down 1.16% year on year) and spend per head £20.01, up £0.38 (1.92%) week on week but down £2.33 (10.4%) year on year.
Sales were £40,924.62, down £740.90 (1.75%) week on week and £3,768.38 (8.4%) year on year, and £4,324.62 (11.82%) above the £36,600 target.
Deliveroo was quieter by nearly £2,000 (£11,274.69 against £12,933.10 on the GM/HC notes; £12.0k against £13.9k on the BOH sheet), so more of the week's sales were taken in restaurant.
Drinks and sides continue to be strong, but sushi sales are still heavily hit by the £5 and free ramen offers (targets 10%, 20% and 13.5%).
Labour was 21.40%, 0.60% under target, with a FOH and BOH split of 43.62% and 56.38% against a 45% and 55% target.

Food cost rose to 25.56% from 23.79%; the site expected to be over budget after ordering frozen ramen and limiting LWC orders, and Jack finds food and labour hard to control with the 40% off over £50 delivery discount and loyalty app redemptions.
Food usage variance was minus 3.2%, wet usage variance 2.6% and total variance minus 2.5%.

Trade peaks with large student groups from roughly 17:00 to 20:00 with quiet hours either side, and takings of about £5k come in on days Jack expects £7k; Penny agreed every site needs a minimum kitchen setup at quiet times.

Hot kitchen waits, particularly for ramen, reached 20 minutes on Deliveroo, which the KPI report calls unacceptable; Harry is looking to expand the ramen prep and service area and Jack is to work with the chefs on faster processes.
The site received eleven 5 star, two 4 star and one 3 star Google reviews; the 3 star left no comment and there were no BOH complaints.
Weekly hygiene compliance scored 100% against the 95% target on the GM/HC notes, and pest control, fire, electrical, gas and ventilation are up to date.
Maintenance: a new lantern is broken, the flickering light on table 102 remains, the toilet taps have been replaced, and Kris wants to do touch up painting once the site buys the paint.
Next week's budget rota is to be finalised by end of day 14/10 with the following two weeks drafted.
Upselling sushi and pushing for more reviews are the stated areas for improvement, alongside Deliveroo prep time as the main priority for everyone on site this week.
Slerp timings need fixing, and the Slerp changeover, XOXO and the Maki App are also upcoming.

Region: five of the nine Scotland and Newcastle sites ran food cost above 25% (Maki 12, 1, 7, 3 and 8), which the Scotland BOH meeting of 13/10 linked to loyalty programme and delivery platform discounts across the group.

Region: new tonkotsu and chicken broth arrives from 15/10 and needs no added water; defrost it a day ahead and reheat it in a pot rather than straight on the heat, and a digital Brix meter is arriving to replace checking by eye, though not every site has one yet (Scotland BOH meeting 13/10).

Region: new chicken arrives on 15/10 and the new char siu (different shape) and pre cooked frozen beef from 19/10, starting at Maki 8; defrost the beef a day ahead and grill or pan fry it for 15 seconds a side before slicing, holding extra stock because it cannot be used on the day it arrives (Scotland BOH meeting 13/10).

Region: the frozen ramen promotion is postponed by one week, and Penny is checking with Michael whether frozen ramen counts in food cost or separately, as some sites have already bought it (Scotland BOH meeting 13/10).
Site efficiency was 92 and delivery sales were close to £11,000 (AM Updates 14/10).

Harry and Ka Ho want a stainless steel flip table in the BOH to double delivery order loads to eight and cut prep time; it is a five minute job for Chris once Michael and Jun approve (AM Updates 14/10).

Region: Ka Ho put food cost of 25.3% to 27.2% at Maki 1, Fountainbridge, M7, M8 and M12 down to promotions lifting usage while sales projections were not adjusted; Michael said site leaders can ask for food cost and wage budget increases (AM Updates 14/10).
Region: a level 8 Halloween ramen with a super spicy factory chilli paste is launching with a video; one bag per site, about a teaspoon per bowl (AM Updates 14/10).
Region: snooze out of stock items on both Deliverect and the POS, or the whole delivery order fails (AM Updates 14/10).
Region: wage revenue baseline is 21% with up to 2% leeway; drinks cost moves to management, food cost to head chefs, new OKRs due end of November (AM Updates 14/10).
